summary: Andreas Larsen's page for Monoid, an open-source coding font, set entirely in Monoid: a typed-on wordmark, a three-column grid of terse facts, and a settings form (alternates, line height, tracking, ligatures) that both restyles a long syntax-highlighted code preview below and builds the custom download. The whole page is essentially one code-playground plus build configurator.

instances.look: 'Monoid' in bold dark-grey monospace at ~200px centred on white, 'Open Source Coding Font' in the oblique at ~50px directly underneath, nothing else
instances.ux: The name and subtitle type themselves on letter by letter after load (blank screen, then 'Monoi', then 'Monoid' + subtitle within ~2s)
instances.learn: For a coding font, type the wordmark on like a terminal: the reveal itself says 'monospaced, for typing'

reconstruction.layout: ~85vh white header, name and subtitle centred as a block ~730px wide, slightly above the middle
reconstruction.typography: Name ~200px Monoid Bold, tight tracking, #2f2f2f; subtitle ~50px Monoid Italic (oblique), same colour, letter-spaced by the monospace grid
reconstruction.behaviour: Typewriter reveal: #h1load and #h3load overlays shrink to uncover the letters in steps (≈0.15s per character), the h3 after the h1
reconstruction.html: header > div > h1 'Monoid' + div#h1load; h3 'Open Source Coding Font' + div#h3load

instances.look: A three-column grid of eight short fact cards in small Monoid: Concept, Features, Support, Monoisome, Ligatures (with the ligature list inline: <!-- -> => <=> == != && :: ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ …), Media, Open Source, Readme; bold headings, one or two lines each, blue links
instances.feel: Like a README rendered as a page
instances.ux: Links to Font Awesome, Medium articles, GitHub issues, licence and readme
instances.learn: State a coding font's whole pitch as one-line specs (size it's hinted for, glyph count, ligatures listed in the font itself) in a grid instead of prose

reconstruction.layout: Content width ~1340px starting at x=64; 3 equal columns (~400px, 60px gutters); rows ~150px; each card = h2 then p
reconstruction.typography: Headings ~18px Monoid Bold; body ~13px Monoid Regular, leading ~1.4, #2f2f2f; links blue; the Monoisome card shows Font Awesome icons rendered inline via the Monoisome font
reconstruction.content: 'Monoid is customizable and optimized for coding with bitmap-like sharpness at 12px/9pt even on low res displays.' / '>750 latin, greek, cyrillic, ligature, alternate and Powerline glyphs'

instances.look: Under the fact grid, a 'Preview' card (Theme: White Light Dark Black; Example: test c py swift js less html) and the 'v0.61' settings form (Alternates $ 0 1 l, LineHeight XS S M L XL, Tracking Tight ½Tight Normal ½Loose Loose, Ligatures On Off) drive a full-width ~3000px dark code view: the Pango language sample table in C with orange strings and grey italic comments, ending in a 'Jump back up' link
instances.ux: Click a theme to recolour the code view; click an example to swap the file (Swift, Python, JS, LESS, HTML, C); 'test' is an empty contenteditable editor ('Type or paste your own code here… characters with alternates: $ * 0 1 3 l'); alternate checkboxes, line-height and tracking radios and the ligature switch restyle the preview live and persist (garlic.js); a pink fixed alert warns that alternates and ligature-off previews fail in Safari/iOS; 'Jump back up' returns to #settings
instances.learn: Wire the download options and the preview to the same controls: the visitor sees their exact build (alternates, spacing, ligatures) in real code before downloading it

reconstruction.layout: Controls inside the grid's last row (Preview card in col 3, settings in col 1 with three blue buttons); code view full-bleed, ~3070px tall for the C example, 64px left padding, pre with natural line breaks; 'Jump back up' centred on white below
reconstruction.typography: Controls ~13px Monoid, inactive options light grey, active underlined/dark; code ~12px Monoid Regular, comments Monoid Italic; syntax colours: strings orange, comments grey, keywords pale
reconstruction.behaviour: Theme spans set a class on #codewrapper (white/light/dark/black highlight.js themes); data-tab spans show one .code pane; checkboxes ss01/ss03/ss05/ss08 and radio calt/nocalt toggle font-feature-settings; lh and fw radios set line-height and letter-spacing steps; state saved by garlic.js (data-persist)
reconstruction.content: Real code files (Async.swift by Tobias Due Munk, the Pango C language sample table with a pangram per language, Bootstrap HTML) plus an empty paste-your-own-code pane
reconstruction.html: #themechooser > span#white|#light|#dark|#black; span.tabs > span[data-tab=test|ccode|python|swift|javascript|less|html]; form[data-persist=garlic] > input#ss01/#ss03/#ss05/#ss08[type=checkbox], input[name=lh] radios, input[name=fw] radios, input#calt/#nocalt; div#codewrapper > div.code#ccode > pre > code.hljs; div#test div#txt[contenteditable]; div#jump > a[href=#settings]; div#safari.alert

instances.look: The 'v0.61' form (version number as heading) with tiny option rows and three small blue buttons: Download, Monoisome, GitHub; after Download, a full-screen modal (captured offscreen) shows a thank-you written as code: 'if (tweeted || facebooked) { gratitude += 1; } if (githubStarred) { karmaBalance = true; } else { $('we').say('ok'); }'
instances.ux: The chosen alternates, line height, tracking and ligature setting select which pre-built variant zip Download fetches; Monoisome downloads the Font Awesome-merged TTF from GitHub; the post-download overlay links 'tweeted', 'facebooked', 'githubStarred' to share intents and the repo, × closes it
instances.learn: Ask for the share after the download, and phrase it in the audience's language (a code snippet): it reads as a wink rather than a nag

reconstruction.layout: Form in the grid's first column (~400px); option rows 18px apart with label then inline toggles; buttons 32px tall in a row; modal: full-viewport overlay with ~108px code text centred, × top-right
reconstruction.typography: Heading 'v0.61' ~18px Monoid Bold; options ~13px; buttons ~12px white on blue; modal code ~108px Monoid Regular with link words underlined
reconstruction.behaviour: #download click → builds the URL of the matching pre-built zip from the checked options, starts the download and shows #postdownload; #close hides it
reconstruction.content: Option labels are the glyphs themselves ($ 0 1 l) rather than feature names
reconstruction.html: section#settings > h2 'v0.61' + form > span#dloptions … + span.noselect.default > a.button#download + a.button (Monoisome) + a.button (GitHub); div#postdownload > div#close + p
